subject: Private offer packaging: tiered usage buffer & distributor fee carveout
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudnexus.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Private offer packaging question: tiered usage buffer & distributor fee

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — CloudNexus is excited about the private offer path for our enterprise bundle. Procurement has a couple of packaging/crediting asks before we lock the PO:

1) Tiered usage buffer: our estimated usage can spike 30-40% month-over-month early in the contract. We need a short-term buffer that won’t immediately push us to an overage rate in month 1. Can Redwood include a 20% buffer for the first two billing cycles (or an equivalent credit)?

2) Distributor fee carveout: we work with a distributor/reseller who requires a 2% pass-through on list price. For marketplace private offers we need that distributor retention to be carved out of the Redwood net so we can reconcile with their invoicing.

3) Margin waterfall transparency: our finance team will need a simple mapping showing list price -> private offer discount -> distributor holdback -> reseller passback -> Redwood net. If you can share a brief workbook that shows the math, that’ll help speed approvals.

I’ve attached the current SOW for context. Can you confirm whether these carveouts are feasible and what, if any, trade-offs there are on SLA/commit sizing?

Attachments: CloudNexus_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 240KB)

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudNexus
procurement@cloudnexus.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudnexus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer packaging question: tiered usage buffer & distributor fee

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. Short answers up front: yes on a short-term buffer (we usually model that as a prepaid credit applied against month 1–2 overages) and yes on supporting a distributor carveout, but we need to align on where the carveout is applied in the waterfall (gross vs list price).

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send a simple workback today showing list price -> discounts -> distributor holdback -> reseller passback -> Redwood net.
- Can we schedule a 30-min sync with finance/procurement this week to lock the exact numbers and sign the PO? I’ve CC’d Ben (channel) and Irene (ops/finance) to scope any implementation constraints.

Quick notes on trade-offs:
- Buffer as a prepaid credit: easiest operationally, preserves SLAs, but increases upfront cash commitment.
- Buffer as temporary uplift to committed usage: reduces cash but complicates metering/true-up.
- Distributor carveout: we can apply it as an explicit line item deducted before reseller passback; channel will need the distributor tax ID and invoicing cadence to automate settlement.

I’ve attached a working workbook (PO_workback_v1.xlsx) that lays out two scenarios: prepaid credit and commit uplift. Review and we’ll refine in the sync.

Attachments: PO_workback_v1.xlsx (Excel)

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: CloudNexus - suggested margin/pass-through for PO DNX-4837

Team — looping you in. CloudNexus wants a 20% short-term buffer and a 2% distributor carveout. I sketched two possible splits in the workbook; summary below:

Scenario A (prepaid buffer):
- List price: $1,000,000 annual equivalent
- Private offer discount (negotiated): 22% -> $780,000
- Distributor holdback (2% of list): $20,000
- Reseller passback (15% of remainder after discount): ~ $117,000
- Redwood net: $643,000

Scenario B (commit uplift):
- List price (committed with 20% uplift first two months encoded): net similar but timing shifts; lower upfront cash from customer, more complex true-up.

Notes / ops constraints:
- If we carve the distributor fee off list price, partner invoicing remains simple but downstream reporting needs a new line in billing exports. Ops (Irene) — can we add a distributor_holdback column to the billing CSV pipeline?
- If finance prefers prepaid credit, we will need to reflect that as a credit memo during onboarding.

Ask: Ben, recommend whether we can standardize distributor carveout at 2% for marketplace private offers or whether we need to treat CloudNexus as an exception. Vanessa, if there are partner program impacts to consider (commissioning, MDF), flag them.

Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: CloudNexus - suggested margin/pass-through for PO DNX-4837

Agree with the approach. A few practical clarifications:
- Reseller passback: 15% is fine as a starting point for a premium channel (their margin demands are high), but we should model a 12% floor if we need to compress for enterprise scale.
- Distributor holdback at 2%: ok to standardize if the distributor provides invoicing evidence net of taxes.
- Billing/export change: Irene, if ops can add a distributor_holdback column, that will make downstream GL reconciliation trivial.

I attached a clean version of the margin workback with the 12% floor modeled.

Attachments: channel_margin_workback.xlsx (Excel)

Ben
Senior Channel Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cloudnexus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer packaging question: tiered usage buffer & distributor fee

Alex — thanks for the patience. We ran the scenarios with channel and ops and here’s the proposal we can sign to move forward:

Agreement highlights:
- Short-term buffer: Redwood will apply a prepaid usage credit equivalent to 20% of estimated first-2-month usage. This credit will be deducted from the first true-up invoice if any overage occurs.
- Distributor carveout: Redwood will apply a 2% distributor holdback on list price as an explicit line item in the billing export. Distributor will be required to issue an invoice or remittance advice to CloudNexus monthly for automation.
- Reseller passback: Standard 15% passback to the reseller (CloudNexus) with a 12% floor if contract scale increases beyond $2M ARR.
- Implementation: ops will add distributor_holdback and reseller_passback columns to the billing export for reconciliation.

Attached: updated workback & margin sheet, plus a draft PO. If that looks good we’ll send the DocuSign link. Proposed MAV (mutual action plan):
1) CloudNexus confirms distributor tax ID and invoicing cadence (this week)
2) Redwood ops adds billing columns and shares test export (within 3 business days of confirmation)
3) DocuSign PO execution (target within 5 business days)

Attachments: PO_workback_v1.xlsx, channel_margin_workback.xlsx
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_example (workbook), https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc123

If that timeline works I’ll fire the DocuSign and loop legal for a minimal amendment to the private offer.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
